text:
ashley: heads-up — seeing SM detection + kernel routing mismatch on perf-cluster-3 after driver update. some 86 GPUs are routed to generic_kv for mid seqlens (>=1536). logs/gist: https://gist.redwood.example/sm-probe-1711122334 :thinking_face:

miguel: can you paste the raw probe output from the node? are we parsing compute capability or using major/minor incorrectly?

ashley: pasted probe output below:
```
node: perf-cluster-3/slot7
cudaDriverVersion: 535.54
deviceProps.name: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB
deviceProps.major: 8
deviceProps.minor: 6
sm_raw: 86
tensor_cores: true
bf16_supported: false
fp8_supported: false
kv_cache_capacity_mb: 2048
kernel_choice: generic_kv (fallbacked)
router_decision_reason: seqlen>1024 && bf16_gate==false -> fallback
```

kevin: if bf16_supported is false then our bf16 fastpath gate should block. but sm86+ should still allow tensor-core fp16 fastpath. maybe gating conflated bf16 with any tensor-core path. :thinking:

perf-bot: microbench results for that node (repro run):
```
seqlen=1536, batch=8, model=gptx-7b
fastpath_sm86_kv: p50=28.3ms, p95=61.1ms, tok/s=380
generic_kv: p50=42.7ms, p95=95.4ms, tok/s=240
kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.72
memory_peak_gb: 54.2
```

ashley: that's the perf regression customers saw on long-context chats. routing to generic_kv doubles p95 in some cases. we need to know why router picked generic_kv when hardware looks fine.

miguel: suspect parsing bug: when driver returns deviceProps.major=8 and minor=6 we compute `sm_id = major*10 + minor` and then try to parse sm_id digits — older code treated single-digit minors differently. new drivers sometimes report sm_raw as 86 string and earlier code interpreted it as 8. Edge case: integer math vs string concat.

kevin: also the BF16 query path changed in driver 535 — cudaDeviceSupportsBfloat16 is now behind a capability query that returns false for SXM until a flag is set. so BF16 gate might be falsely off. we should explicitly check tensor_core availability separately from BF16.

yara: config snapshot: `fastpath_seqlen_threshold=1024`, `require_bf16_for_fastpath=false`, `allow_tensorcore_fp16=true`, `kv_prefetch_enabled=true`, `kv_prefetch_max_pages=8`. router code seems to evaluate `if seqlen>=threshold && bf16_supported then fastpath else generic`. that's too strict.

perf-bot: repro run after making router ignore bf16 for fp16 fastpath:
```
seqlen=1536, batch=8
fastpath_sm86_kv (fp16): p50=29.1ms, p95=63.5ms
generic_kv: p50=42.6ms, p95=96.0ms
delta: ~+40% p50 improvement when fastpath used
```

ashley: concrete plan: 1) fix SM parsing to robustly handle major/minor and string sm_raw; 2) split fastpath gates into two checks: tensor-core fp16 allowed (no bf16 required) and bf16-specific fastpath; 3) add unit tests for driver 535 and 537 edge cases; 4) telemetry: log `kernel_choice` + `gate_reasons` on cold start.

miguel: agree. also add a small safety: if kv_cache_capacity_mb < model_kv_minimum then force generic_kv even if fastpath ok (we saw cache-thrashing at seqlen=4096 on low-mem instances).

kevin: can we also add a fallback warm-up that tries fastpath for N requests and rolls back if error/regressions seen? avoids full rollout risk.

yara: note for rollout checklist: add perf smoke test (p50/p95/tok/s) and kv-eviction counter check. i'll update runbook. :white_check_mark:

ashley: i'll open PR with patch + tests. will include profiling harness and add a short-lived feature flag `force_fastpath_probe` to flip on for canary nodes.

perf-bot: action items created: PERF-3721 (fix sm parse + gates), PERF-3722 (telemetry kernel_choice), PERF-3723 (kv eviction metric).

miguel: thanks. one more: add a small probe at startup that validates chosen kernel by running a tiny matmul to confirm tensor core path doesn't crash (non-blocking, times out after 200ms). better to detect hardware-driver mismatches early.

ashley: adding that test to PR too. will post PR link when ready. :thumbsup:

kevin: thanks team — assigning reviews and canary plan in the PR.

yara: ack.
